quote: Lately, I feel like I've been scrambling to reschedule and keep track of payments, so I plan to transition my studio to My Music Staff since my studio has quickly grown to 28 students in only 6 months.
I also charge by the month and do not give discounts for missed lessons, and I also allow for makeup lessons if given advance notice, so texting is part of my admin time every week.
I could cut that out by having a no make-up, no reschedule policy, I suppose, but I don't like that for a number of reasons.
Mom has asked already three times to reschedule lessons that she has missed because...reasons.
The tighter your schedule, the harder it is to put in makeup lessons.
I have requested makeups, I never really hear back from this teacher about them, she claims it's too difficult to schedule and they never happen.
Doing the swap list thing for any client willing to be on the list may be a possibility that would take the rearranging out of my hands.
Sometimes, people ask to pay late because they don't have the money.
However, she has now decided that she'll pay me at the end of the month after the lessons are already done, rather than the start.
Do you really want the hassle of recording and depositing 25 - 35 people a week/100 - 120 per month?
To remind people, you would have to tell them outside of Venmo.
The pay up front each month is really the easiest way to keep straight (receipts and record keeping- ugh!)
I have trepidation about charging a set fee per month of lessons (with the number of lessons being variable).
I think my clients would be pretty unhappy if I told them I were charging for 4.5 lessons per month.
So some months will have 5 lessons but others might only have 3, or even only 2 if there is a school holiday.
A good friend of mine has argued vehemently against providing lessons in the fifth week.
The biggest issue is the app should allow teachers to go in and fix practice times when student forgets to stop practice timer.
It doesn’t allow any edit on practice time/date so parents can make edit to accurately reflect the kids practice.
QOL need: Please let us input a practice time without the timer.
Plus, their prices for monthly subscription are going up substantially and unless these issues are fixed, I don’t think it’s worth that monthly fee.
I have looked into these in the past, but I found that it wasn't very difficult to do so for free.
I believe she uses a program called Microsoft Excel, which has always been sufficient for our needs.
I already own Quickbooks for my business, so I email invoices.
Financially, I use checks and Venmo.
Better yet, Notion is cheaper than studio software.
If you don’t pay close attention to your outgoing cash, it’s very easy in 2026 for recurring subscriptions to keep quietly pulling those fees every month.
Some of my favorite things: parents can reschedule their lessons without contacting me directly, auto-invoicing, make-up lesson credits, and enforcement of cancellation policies.

When we heard last September that Tonara would be closing down, I knew I wanted to find an app to replace it, and I wanted to make the move quickly so that I could save as much assignment history as possible in the new app.
I’ve been using Tonara since it came out and I will be looking for a replacement for it.
I ended up picking My Music Staff mainly for their business features even though Tonara did seem like a better student-facing practice app.
After much deliberation—and denial—I ended up switching to Practice Space.
